(i) fusion at the feature level is better than fusion at the output level, (ii) fusion of face and body information is better than face-only or body-only recognition, and (iii) the proposed fusion method can be used for the recognition of the six universal emotions (anger, happiness, sadness, fear, disgust and surprise).

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the best recognition performance is achieved with early fusion, which combines information from both modalities before the classification stage, in comparison to late fusion, in which information from both modalites is combined after the individual modalities have been classified.
fusion of facial and bodily information is better than using facial information only, and fusion at a feature-level is better than fusion at a decision-level.
the best recognition performance is achieved by the fusion of facial expression and body gesture at the feature-level.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of both facial expression and body gesture in an early fusion approach can improve the recognition accuracy of visual emotion recognition.
the fusion of the face and body modalities is a promising way to improve the accuracy of emotion recognition.
fusion of face and body information can lead to a more accurate emotion recognition than the use of the face modality alone.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the field of emotion recognition, the fusion of different modalities can lead to better performance than using the individual modalities.
the fusion of facial expression and body gesture modalities can be beneficial for the recognition of affective states.
